symptom: Excessive White / Brown Foam in Aeration Tank
root_cause: Un-degraded detergents/surfactants in raw dyeing effluent or low F/M ratio causing Nocardia filamentous growth.
immediate_action_rule: Spray water nozzles over aeration surface immediately to collapse foam. Dose food-grade silicone antifoam at 5-10 ppm.
preventive_rule: Increase Wasted Activated Sludge (WAS) rate to decrease sludge age; ensure equalization tank retains surfactant shock loads.

symptom: Sludge Bulking / Poor Settling in Secondary Clarifier (SVI > 180 mL/g)
root_cause: Prolonged low DO (< 1.0 mg/L), low pH (< 6.5), or nitrogen deficiency encouraging filamentous bacterial dominance.
immediate_action_rule: Dose Hydrogen Peroxide (10-20 mg/L) or Sodium Hypochlorite (2-3 kg Chlorine/1000 kg MLSS) into RAS pipe to kill external filaments.
preventive_rule: Increase aeration blower output to maintain DO > 2.5 mg/L; dose Urea/DAP to satisfy BOD:N:P = 100:5:1.

symptom: Pin Flocs Escalating in Secondary Clarifier Overflow
root_cause: Over-aeration (DO > 4.5 mg/L) shearing bio-flocs or old sludge age (MCRT > 20 days).
immediate_action_rule: Reduce aeration blower frequency by 15-20% to decrease shear stress.
preventive_rule: Increase sludge wasting rate to bring sludge age back down to 10-12 days.

symptom: Sudden Drop in Aeration Tank MLSS (< 2000 mg/L)
root_cause: Toxic chemical shock load (heavy metals, peroxide, caustic surge) killing bio-culture or excessive sludge wasting.
immediate_action_rule: Immediately stop sludge wasting. Divert toxic feed to emergency holding tank. Add fresh cow dung / municipal seed sludge.
preventive_rule: Ensure strict automated pH/temperature shutdown valves at Equalization outlet.

symptom: High Color Leakage in Primary Clarifier Overflow
root_cause: Incorrect coagulant pH or wrong coagulant dosage for hydrolyzed reactive dyes.
immediate_action_rule: Adjust pH to optimum 6.8 using H2SO4; increase PAC dosage by 50 mg/L or introduce Ferrous Sulfate.
preventive_rule: Conduct jar tests every 4 hours or upon dye bath discharge changes.

symptom: Rapid Rise in RO Membrane Differential Pressure (ΔP > 2.5 bar)
root_cause: Bio-fouling or organic fouling on RO membrane surface due to high SDI or bacterial leak from UF.
immediate_action_rule: Perform high-pH Clean-In-Place (CIP) with 0.1% NaOH + 0.1% EDTA solution at 35°C for 2 hours.
preventive_rule: Replace UF module filters; increase SMBS dosing to ensure zero chlorine and sanitize feed lines weekly.

symptom: Scaling on RO High-Pressure Stage Membranes
root_cause: Precipitation of Calcium Sulfate (CaSO4) or Silica due to depleted antiscalant dosing or exceeding recovery threshold.
immediate_action_rule: Perform low-pH Clean-In-Place (CIP) with 2% Citric Acid or 0.5% HCl solution for 3 hours.
preventive_rule: Check antiscalant pump flow; restrict recovery rate to maximum design envelope based on projection software.

symptom: Severe Foaming and Boiling Instability in MEE (Multiple Effect Evaporator)
root_cause: High residual COD / organic carryover in RO Reject feed entering evaporator.
immediate_action_rule: Dose food-grade polyglycol defoamer directly into 1st effect MEE recirculation line. Lower steam supply pressure.
preventive_rule: Ensure Fenton/Ozone tertiary treatment reduces RO Reject COD to < 300 mg/L before feed to MEE.
